questions.question: Sujit Mukherjee proposes a "three-literature scheme" for college / graduates. What are the three literary areas this scheme would give them access to?
questions.solution_html:
• Sujit Mukherjee suggests a a “three-literature scheme” for college students to enjoy literature –
  • helps students read and understand stories from different places - three literary areas : Literature
  • in the student's own language - other Indian language literatures in English translation - World
  • literature in English translation - practical in India - students know one Indian language well and
  • use English in college - helps students explore their own culture, other Indian and world cultures.
questions.final_answer: use English in college - helps students explore their own culture, other Indian and world cultures

questions.question: Examine the theme of love and obsession in Angela's seventeen-year / correspondence with Bayardo San Román.
questions.solution_html:
• Ángela Vicario marries Bayardo San Román - Bayardo returns her on wedding night for not being
  • a virgin – Angela begins to love him and writes one letter every week without stop, even with no
  • reply from him - thinks only of Bayardo, works on embroidery, and letters become her whole
  • world - hopeless, yet writing turns into deep obsession born from pain and honour - Bayardo
  • comes back after 17 years with all her letters in bundles—none opened—showing strange, late
  • love.
questions.final_answer: love
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What does the panther's repetitive pacing suggest about its mental and / emotional state?
questions.solution_html:
• "Der Panther"- by Rainer Maria Rilke - repetitive pacing of the panther walks in a small circle
  • not free movement like in the wild - like a ritual with no change – inside, the mighty will is
  • paralyzed and hopeless - eyes see nothing - feels like a thousand bars and no world behind them
  • real world is lost - only cage and circle - no memory stays - mental and emotional state - alive
  • but not living - mind is empty and tired.
questions.final_answer: but not living - mind is empty and tired
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Who is the Beggar Woman in Blood Wedding, and what symbolic role / does she play?
questions.solution_html:
• An old woman in black clothes - appears in Act III near the house and in the forest - speaks to the
  • Mother, Neighbour, Leonardo, the Bride - Symbolisms: She is Death - smells blood and says
  • men will kill - opens the door for Death and helps find the men - shows fate - knows the tragedy
  • from the start. - a messenger of doom - part of dark nature - belongs to the moon, forest, and
  • magic world - supernatural - Death in human form.
questions.final_answer: magic world - supernatural - Death in human form
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Compare and contrast the portrayal of Santiago Nasar in Chapter 2 (at / the wedding) with Chapter 3 (his final night at Maria Alejandrina Cervantes's).
questions.solution_html:
• Chronicle of a Death Foretold - Gabriel García Márquez - Chapter 2 – Wedding (Public Glory)
  • Santiago wears white suit and silver tie - 21, tall, slim, handsome - a rich, charming hero - dances
  • with Angela, drinks, laughs, gives gifts - centre of the party - no worry about danger - Chapter 3
  • – Maria’s House (Private Pain) - after party, he is drunk and tired - sleeps only one hour - goes to
  • brothel for love and sin - Sad and Secret Side - long-time lover of Maria - sings love songs - feels
  • empty and alone - Similarities: Both chapters show young, attractive and kind Santiago - people
  • love him -Differences and Question: Wedding - perfect public mask - Who was the real
  • Santiago?
questions.final_answer: Santiago?
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How does the setting of the short story The Guest communicate the / political situation in Algeria?
questions.solution_html:
• Setting – a lonely plateau – tells us about war, fear, and no escape - Daru's school is far from
  • villages. No people or help - French control is weak - Arabs hide and fight. - sudden October
  • snow after long drought - Nature is cruel like the war. - children stop school - Daru alone - two
  • roads at the end of the story: East - prison (French law), South - desert freedom (Arab tribes) - no
  • middle way. country split by war - empty, cold land - broken Algeria - no safety or friendship
  • only hard choices between rule and revolt.
questions.final_answer: only hard choices between rule and revolt
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How is the garden a symbol for futility of choices?
questions.solution_html:
• Garden - name of a strange book made by Ts’ui Pên, the ancestor of Yu Tsun - a labyrinth – a maze
  • of time, not space - in Ts’ui Pên’s garden, all choices happen together - man fights, runs, dies and
  • lives, all at the same time - every page splits into many futures - book has no end - keeps forking
  • forever - futile - too many paths - no real choice - Time is chaos - Future is fixed with all
  • outcomes -Book has no end - choices are illusion.
questions.final_answer: outcomes -Book has no end - choices are illusion
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss how cultural theorists such as Raymond Williams and Stuart / Hall supported polysystem approaches and contributed to rethinking translation in cultural contexts.
questions.solution_html:
• Polysystem Theory: Literature is part of a big system with high and low art. Translated books
  • fight for space in this system - Raymond Williams - Culture is ordinary daily life, not only great
  • books/works - Translators are culture makers - bring new voices - Rethinking translation - old
  • view: Translation = copy original - Williams’ view - Translation - new culture event - adds to the
  • system. Stuart Hall - Meaning is not fixed - writer codes message - reader decodes - Translator
  • decodes original culture, then recodes for new readers - Meaning changes - readers accept, change
  • or reject meaning. - Rethinking translation - Translation is not a perfect copy - negotiation between
  • cultures - Both support Polysystem - Williams: Translation joins big culture system. Hall
  • Translation changes meaning in new place.
questions.final_answer: Translation changes meaning in new place
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How does The Albatross mark the transition between Romanticism and / Symbolism in European poetry?
questions.solution_html:
• “The Albatross” - change from Romanticism to Symbolism - stands between two big poetry styles
  • - a bridge poem. Romantic aspect - Poet as Hero - loved nature and freedom - albatross is “king of
  • the sky” and “prince of the clouds” - flies high in storms and laughs at the archer (danger) - brave
  • free spirit - beautiful and majestic in the air. Symbolist aspect – hidden meaning and pain - uses
  • one image - albatross is not just a bird - Transition from dream to real world: Romanticism - poet
  • escapes to nature and imagination. - Symbolism - poet trapped in city, society, cruelty - “The
  • Albatross” shows both: Sky (Romantic) → free, high, stormy - Ship deck (Symbolist) → cruel
  • men, jokes, shame. - This change symbolises modern poetry – where art shows inner truth, not just
  • nature. Baudelaire opens the door from dreams to symbols.
questions.final_answer: nature. Baudelaire opens the door from dreams to symbols
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What does Natalya say to insult Ivan?
questions.solution_html:
• Natalya insults Ivan Lomov during their arguments - hurt Ivan's feelings and health - calls him bad
  • names - shows her strong temper - small fights ruin big plans. First Fight: argue over who owns
  • Oxen meadows - Second Fight: about hunting dogs - Natalya's words are funny but her insults
  • show how people fight over small things like land and pets - Ivan is weak and shy -Natalya is loud
  • and proud. Chekhov uses this to laugh at marriage and neighbours. In the end, they marry anyway
  • – love wins, but fights do not stop.
questions.final_answer: – love wins, but fights do not stop
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How does the wife’s version of events differ from the others, and what / does it show about her situation?
questions.solution_html:
• Seven people tell the police what happened in the bamboo forest – Masago’s words show her
  • shame, fear, and lost honour – Woodcutter, Priest, Policeman, Mother - only see outside things – dead
  • body, rope, comb, horse - do not know the full story. Bandit Tajōmaru says he raped Masago, then
  • fought the husband with swords - won after 23 blows - Masago asked him to kill her husband and ran
  • away - Tajōmaru freed him - husband felt hate in her eyes – later someone stabbed him with a small
  • dagger while he was tied again. Masago’s Story – big differences: Tajōmaru left quickly after the
  • rape. He did not fight the husband - Husband’s eyes - she saw cold hate in his face - looked at her like
  • dirty trash – killed her husband – tried to kill herself - but is still alive, hiding in Kiyomizu Temple
  • cannot live with shame - cannot die - trapped between life and death - takes blame - Women have no
  • voice - men speak of swords and pride - she speaks of pain, guilt, and silence - a woman crushed by
  • rules - her pain is real.
questions.final_answer: rules - her pain is real
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
